answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging each new identity an inlet fee paid in escrowed reputation rather than cash: every newcomer must be sponsored by a peer who locks part of its own score, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer is later shown to be a puppet. Fake identities then drain the sponsor, so the opal-thin margin of a mass farm disappears, while honest agents still reach the kernel of trusted participants through gradual, audited work.
